title: The Lord's Day
hookLine: every Sunday is a little Easter

lines: THE FIRST DAY OF THE WEEK.
cards: It's very early. A few women are walking out of Jerusalem carrying spices, worried about one practical thing: who will roll the stone away from the tomb? The Sabbath is over.
It's the first day of the week, and the sun is coming up. When they get there, Mark says, the stone is already rolled back, and the tomb is empty.
Out of that one morning, Christians built a habit that comes round every week.

teach.h: THE FIRST DAY OF THE WEEK.
teach.b: Each of the four Gospels puts the empty tomb early on the first day of the week, so the first day became the Christians' day.
In Acts, the disciples at Troas, with Paul visiting, gather on the first day of the week to break bread. And the last book of the Bible gives the day its name.

teach.h: I WAS IN THE SPIRIT ON THE LORD'S DAY.
teach.b: John, on the island of Patmos, writes in the Douay-Rheims: "I was in the spirit on the Lord's day." In the Latin of the Church, Sunday is still Dominica, the Lord's.

Justin Martyr, writing to the Roman emperor, described the day called Sunday: Christians gathered from town and country, heard the writings of the apostles and prophets, prayed, and shared bread and wine, and a collection went to widows and orphans.
Catholics reading it today recognize the Mass. Catholics speak of every Sunday as a little Easter: not a reminder of Easter, they say, but the same feast, coming round every seven days.
The Second Vatican Council called Sunday the original feast day, the foundation of the whole year.

teach.h: THE EIGHTH DAY: A NEW CREATION.
teach.b: Some early writers called it the eighth day: the old week ended with the Sabbath, the seventh, and they saw the resurrection as the first day of a new creation, outside the old count.
Catholics keep it two ways: Mass, which the Church asks of them as an obligation, and rest, setting aside work that gets in the way of worship, joy and family.
Pope John Paul the Second wrote a whole letter on it in 1998, Dies Domini, the day of the Lord.

teach.h: A LITTLE EASTER, EVERY SEVEN DAYS.
teach.b: And week ninety-nine ends here: the Lateran, Christ the King, the months with their themes, then Friday, the Ember days, Mary's Saturday, and now Sunday, the day the whole week leans toward.

how: Catholics are asked to attend Mass every Sunday (or on Saturday evening) and to keep the day free of work that hinders worship, rest and time with family; many families also keep a shared Sunday meal.

o: Latin for a Mass said by a bishop
Latin for the Sabbath, the seventh day
Latin for the Lord's: the name for Sunday

games.q: the Lord's day — tap the pairs.

s: Christians chose Sunday because it was the Jewish Sabbath
the Sabbath is Saturday. Sunday was chosen because the tomb was found empty on the first day of the week.
the name the Lord's day appears in the Bible
John writes it in the Book of Revelation: I was in the spirit on the Lord's day.
some early Christian writers called Sunday the eighth day
the first day of a new creation, outside the old count of seven.

games.q: you're one of the first Christians. the resurrection happened on the first day of the week. which day do you gather?
o: only once a year, at Passover.
the first day of the week, every week.
games.why: Acts shows them gathering on the first day of the week to break bread. Easter came round every seven days.

practice: Picture next Sunday from morning to night, with its noise, its errands, its inbox.
Choose one thing to set down that day, a chore that can wait, a screen, a worry for Monday, and one thing to put in its place: a long meal, a walk, a call to someone you love, Mass if you go.

wordCard.voice: Dominica. Latin for the Lord's, the Church's own name for Sunday since John called it the Lord's day in Revelation. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: the Lord's day, from Revelation 1:10.

carryVoice: Your line: a little easter. Every seven days, that same morning comes round. Day six hundred ninety-three.
